name: Aqualyx

card.summary: A deoxycholate injectable sold in Europe for localized fat; its use for facial hollowing in forums goes beyond any clinical evidence.
card.note: Not FDA-approved; counterfeit and DIY use have been associated with infection and nodule reports.

quick.overview:
Aqualyx is a CE-marked injectable made from deoxycholic acid, a bile acid that dissolves fat cell membranes. In Europe it is sold to trained practitioners for reducing small pockets of fat such as under the chin.

In looksmaxxing forums it is discussed as a way to slim the cheeks, jaw and neck area. Published clinical evidence for these uses is limited to small studies and case reports, and no published trial has tested facial-hollowing as described in forums.
quick.mechanism: Deoxycholate acts as a detergent on fat cell membranes, causing cells to break open; the body then clears the debris, with inflammation and later fibrosis described in the treated area. The related drug Kybella is the US-approved deoxycholic acid product for submental fat.
quick.risks: Reported effects are swelling, bruising and pain. A published case described chronic infection and nodule formation after a deoxycholate injection. The product is not FDA-approved, counterfeits have been discussed in forums, and the manufacturer sells only to trained professionals; self-injection is outside labelled use.

lead: Aqualyx is a gel-like aqueous solution of sodium deoxycholate, developed in Italy by Professor Pasquale Motolese and commercially available since 2009, marketed by Marllor and sold to doctors and nurses trained in intralipotherapy [2][1]. It is CE-marked in the European Union and used for localized subcutaneous fat [1][2].
Deoxycholic acid is a naturally occurring bile acid; the US FDA has approved a different deoxycholic acid product, Kybella, for submental fat [3]. Aqualyx has no FDA approval [1].

Published studies of Aqualyx are limited. One empirical study examined ultrasound-guided injection for lipomas [4], and a case report described chronic infection and nodules after a deoxycholate injection [2]. In looksmaxxing forums it is discussed for slimming the lower face and neck, an application no published trial has evaluated.

paras: Per Grokipedia, intended targets are small, pinchable pockets of fat such as the chin, abdomen, flanks and thighs [1]. Practitioner-led treatment is described as multiple sessions spaced weeks apart [1].

Deoxycholic acid disrupts the lipid membranes of fat cells, releasing their contents and prompting an inflammatory response in which macrophages clear debris, followed by fibrosis [1]. The US label-approved relative is Kybella, which Wikipedia describes as destroying submental fat cells over several months [3].

Grokipedia lists swelling, bruising and discomfort as common, with infection and nodules reported in some cases [1]. A 2022 case report described chronic infection and nodule formation after injection of an advertised deoxycholate product, noting Aqualyx is sold only to trained clinicians [2].

Users on looksmax.org post threads about price, authenticity and results, with some reporting a persistent hollow look after cheek and neck treatment and others discussing swelling after injection [5]. Threads include warnings about counterfeit products and disputes about whether the outcome is permanent. The wiki does not reproduce dosing or technique details.

A study of ultrasound-guided Aqualyx injection reported on lipoma removal [4]. A 2022 case report documented chronic infection and nodule formation after deoxycholate injection [2]. No published studies were found on Aqualyx for facial hollowing or buccal fat reduction.

timeline.event: Study of ultrasound-guided Aqualyx injection for lipomas published [4].
Case report of chronic infection and nodules after deoxycholate injection [2].

lore.intro: Aqualyx is discussed on looksmax.org as a cheap route to a leaner face, with threads on sourcing, authenticity and results [5].

claims.claim: Aqualyx gives a permanent hollow-cheek look.
claims.believers: Posters share before-and-after images and say the effect persists after the initial swelling subsides [5].
claims.experts: No published trial has tested facial hollowing; the available literature covers other indications [4][1].

claims.believers: Proponents say the cells are lysed and do not regrow.
claims.experts: Grokipedia describes irreversible adipocyte lysis, and Wikipedia describes submental fat cell destruction for the approved relative Kybella [1][3].

claims.claim: Self-injected or imported product is equivalent to clinic treatment.
claims.believers: Some posters report good results from ordered vials.
claims.experts: The manufacturer sells only to trained practitioners [2]; a case report described chronic infection and nodules after deoxycholate injection [2].
